The term "ordinary body" means the natural body. What is this natural body? It is the body of the <term>Tathagata</term> that one can never tire of beholding. What is this body that one can never tire of beholding? It is a body whose complexion is unlike that of humans or gods, and for which there is no equivalent object in the world; such is the complexion possessed by the natural body of the <term>Tathagata</term>.

Everyone knows that although it appears to have a complexion, it is not like the complexion of our own bodies. Similarly, while it possesses flesh, bones, hair, and nails, it is not like that of any other sentient being. Even though it appears in that way, all worldly beings are filled with wonder. Thus, while the body exists as a body and appears in that manner, and while worldly beings are filled with wonder, no one can know what its true nature is.

In this way, although it resembles the bodies of all others in terms of shape, form, and so forth, its nature remains unknown. This body, which is extremely radiant and vast, is called "that which one can never tire of beholding." Alternatively, it is of the nature of <term>vajra</term> <gloss>diamond/thunderbolt</gloss>, or of the nature of gold, jewels, pearls, <term>vaidurya</term> <gloss>lapis lazuli</gloss>, and the like, or it belongs to the category of a human body, or to the category of the body of a god or Brahma.

Among sentient beings in the hell realms, the animal realm, the <term>preta</term> <gloss>hungry ghost</gloss> realm, the <term>asura</term> <gloss>demigod</gloss> realm, and among humans, suffering appears in great abundance. The pure realms of the Buddhas are generally not like this. The aeons are also of a degenerate nature.

Due to the intermediate aeon of famine, the unbearable suffering of famine arises in the world from time to time. Due to the intermediate aeon of disease, many illnesses arise. Due to the intermediate aeon of weapons, much mutual harm and violence arise. Due to the power of destruction by water, the aspect of emotional affliction <term>klesha</term> <gloss>mental defilement</gloss> becomes predominant; due to the power of destruction by fire, the aspect of hatred becomes predominant; and due to the power of destruction by wind, the aspect of ignorance becomes predominant. Thus, many faults of the times arise.

Regarding the degeneration of lifespan, there is no certainty in the lives of sentient beings. At times, the lifespan is immeasurable. At other times, it becomes ten years. Even that is uncertain. Some die while still in the womb. Some die immediately after birth, or during childhood, or in youth, or in the prime of life, or in middle age, or in old age. Because there is no certainty of death, there is much grief, lamentation, suffering, and mental distress in the world.

Regarding the degeneration of views, there are sixty-two types of extremely evil views that destroy all virtue when categorized individually. Those who have firmly entered into wrong views cannot be cured even by a thousand Buddhas. Furthermore, all non-Buddhist practitioners <term>tirthika</term> <gloss>those who hold extreme or wrong views</gloss> are characterized by disparagement, lack of faith, inability to gather in the assembly, and are highly contemptible. They are not vessels for the truth by nature. Their mental continuums have largely become like hot peppers, and their mental continuums have largely become like garlic, lacking the holy Dharma in their minds.

# The Explanation of the Noble Sutra of the Four Dharmas <note>original: "Arya-catur-dharma-vyakhyana"</note>

Homage to Manjushri, the Youthful.

Why was this sutra composed, which states, "A Bodhisattva, a Great Being, should not abandon these four dharmas even for the sake of their life, as long as they live"? It was composed to correctly instruct those who are confused about the methods for attaining unsurpassed enlightenment after having truly entered the Great Vehicle; to cause those who are heedless to truly take hold [of the path]; to truly uplift those who are discouraged; and to cause those who have truly entered [the path] to be truly joyful.

The number "four" is mentioned to avoid [the text] becoming too extensive, thereby preventing those who do not wish to listen from abandoning it. Mentioning the number also makes it easier to remember. The patience and gentleness that appear later are not distinct, as they serve the same purpose.

Although there are many categories for those who have truly entered the Great Vehicle, two names are mentioned for three reasons: through aspiration, through application, and through realization. What is meant by aspiration? One is a "Bodhisattva" because one aspires to profound objects of knowledge. One is a "Great Being" because one aspires to great power. What is meant by application? It is because one strives for the sake of one's own unsurpassed, perfectly complete enlightenment, and because one strives to fully protect all sentient beings from suffering. What is meant by realization? It is because enlightenment is realized through two powers. What are the two? They are the power of wisdom and the power of diligence. Here it is necessary that you follow me, not I you. And although you may still thunder many things against me, my Monarchy shall nevertheless stand, while yours will all perish. I do not write so prolixly about Alchemy in vain, but I do it with this mind and purpose, that from these things you may know closely and solidly what lies hidden within it, and how it ought to be understood. Nor should you be offended by this, that neither gold nor silver comes forth from it: But rather, this must be carefully attended to, that through it secrets <term>arcana</term> <gloss>hidden medicinal powers</gloss> may be uncovered, and the seductions of the <term>seplasiariorum</term> <gloss>perfumers/apothecaries</gloss> be exposed, by which the crude mob is deceived, while they serve them for one florin what they would not redeem for a single coin. Such are their precious secrets.

<margin>Poison even in the best things.</margin>
Who is there who would dare to deny that poison lies hidden and exists even in the best things? All are forced to admit this. If this is therefore true, I now ask you whether poison should not be separated from the good and useful? And the good be accepted, and the evil left behind? Indeed, it is necessary. If, therefore, it is necessary: I ask you to explain to me, how is this separated in your workshops? For among you, all things remain mixed. But in order to defend your simplicity, if you are convicted to admit that poison lies hidden there, and you are asked where it eventually goes: then you bring forth I know not what about "corrections," which supposedly extract and remove the poison,
<margin>The correction of physicians is ventilated.</margin>
just as they correct Quince with Scammony, or after Diagridium <note>a purgative preparation of scammony</note>. But what kind of correction is that? Does the poison not remain afterwards just as it was at first? And yet you meanwhile boast that you have corrected it, so that the poison no longer harms. But where has it gone?
<margin>Diagridion.</margin>
It remains in the Diagridium. Test this, if you are wise: exceed the measure, and you will see where the poison is. For you will know that not sluggishly. Thus you also correct Turbith <note>a purgative root</note>, and call it Diaturbith. Such are your corrections, which would befit rustics and should be given to horses. Make a trial by exceeding the measure, and increase the dose: you will see whether you will not feel the poison.
<margin>What "to correct" means for a physician.</margin>
*To correct is to take what is corrected.* Whoever is malicious and has sinned: if he is punished, the correction does not extend further than the will of the one who has been punished lasts. Such are these corrections too; it is situated with them, not with you. Now, in this case, the physician has nothing more to consider than that the poison be removed. This must be done through separation: as, for example: a serpent is poisonous, and yet it is adopted into food. If you remove the poison from it, you may eat it without any harm. The same must be understood equally regarding all other things, namely that there is a need for a similar separation. That not yet being done, you cannot be secure in your operation: unless by chance it happens that nature supplies your place, or a greater kindness of the heavens favors you. For in your art, no protection will remain.

Now, therefore, at last, if that true foundation is necessary, which removes the poison, how does Alchemy perform this? For it is necessary that this be done in such a way that, if Mars <note>iron</note> is in the Sun <note>gold</note>, Mars is removed, and if Saturn <note>lead</note> is in Venus <note>copper</note>, it is separated from it. For as many ascendants and impressions as there are in the things of nature, so many bodies exist in them. But those bodies which are contrary, it is necessary that some of them be entirely removed and taken away, so that in this way all contrariety may be lifted, and the evil which you seek may be taken away from the good.
<margin>Fire perfects all things.</margin>
As gold is useful for nothing unless it is first cast into the fire: so much less useful is a medicine which does not pass through the fire. For it is necessary that all things pass through fire into another generation, which ought to conduce to and assist man. And should this not deservedly be considered the proper foundation of any physician? For a physician ought not to apply poisons, but true secrets.
<margin>Workshops criticized.</margin>
But all those workshop preparations, however many there are, do not contribute even a letter to this doctrine: but they are occupied simply in correcting, just as if a dog has farted in a room, and that stench is suppressed either by troches and incense, or by juniper wood: I ask, does the stench not remain in the room afterwards just as it did before? And although it may not be perceived by smell: is it therefore permitted for anyone to say that the stench has been separated and no longer remains? Indeed, it is present, but corrected by the fumigation. Thus, therefore, the fumigation and the stench enter the nostrils together. Of this kind also are the corrections of the Pharmacopoeias, who dull the <term>Aleopaticum</term> <gloss>a purgative medicine</gloss> with sugar, so that it may inflict no harm. Yet they boast and sell themselves as the princes of physicians. But who is so stupid that he does not immediately smell that these things are worth nothing? ## CHAPTER II.

**T**here is, therefore, in all metals a true Mercury, and a right sulfur, equally in imperfect as in perfect metals: it has only been made contaminated and impure in imperfect metals, which alone are deprived of perfect maturation. And for the same reasons they can be reduced to gold and silver, that is, so that the impurity with which they had been defiled may be separated from the golden or silver nature that is in them, and the form of gold or silver may be instilled into them. For they have been torn away from nature because they were removed and dug out from natural passages, mines, and veins of the earth: therefore they can no longer have any operation in themselves, as if they were still lying hidden under the earth; nevertheless, however, as much as is in them, they desire to be perfected.
